name: Iglesia vaginal mesh trial
question: Does adding vaginal polypropylene mesh to colpopexy improve anatomic success over traditional vaginal repair without mesh for stage 2–4 prolapse?

design.population: Women with POP-Q stage 2–4 pelvic organ prolapse undergoing vaginal repair.
design.locator: Iglesia 2010, PubMed abstract, Objective, Methods and Results; see notes for conflicting arm counts

verdictNote: No objective cure advantage; enrollment stopped at the prespecified mesh-exposure threshold.
takeaway: Vaginal colpopexy with polypropylene mesh did not improve objective or subjective cure versus traditional vaginal colpopexy without mesh in the early report; enrollment stopped after five mesh exposures (15.6%).

reports.label: Three-month primary report
reports.citation: Iglesia CB, Sokol AI, Sokol ER, et al. "Vaginal mesh for prolapse: a randomized controlled trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2010;116(2 Pt 1):293-303. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e3181e7d7f8
reports.followUp: Three-month primary assessment; median 9.7 months at early stopping (range 2.4–26.7)

results.measure: POP-Q stage 1 or lower at 3 months
results.note: The abstract concludes that objective cure did not differ; it does not give the prespecified comparison's numerical result.

results.measure: Any-compartment recurrence at reported assessment; comparison P=.28
results.note: Abstract prints 59.4% and 70.4%, respectively; the latter does not reconcile with the stated control-arm size.
Outcome denominators are not given in the abstract.

harms.label: Cystotomy
harms.note: The abstract reports two cystotomies in the mesh arm only.

harms.label: Blood transfusion
harms.note: The abstract reports one transfusion in the mesh arm only.

delivery.label: Mesh placement
delivery.value: Among 32 mesh procedures, 24 received anterior mesh and eight received total mesh.

delivery.label: Native-tissue operation
delivery.value: Vaginal colpopexy, primarily uterosacral ligament suspension, with concurrent colporrhaphy.

reports.label: One-year outcomes
reports.citation: Sokol AI, Iglesia CB, Kudish BI, et al. "One-year objective and functional outcomes of a randomized clinical trial of vaginal mesh for prolapse." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2012;206(1):86.e1-9. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2011.08.003
reports.followUpLocator: PubMed abstract, Study Design and Results

results.measure: POP-Q stage 1 or lower at 12 months
results.note: The abstract reports similar recurrence rates and no improvement in one-year cure with mesh.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Study Design, Results and Conclusion

results.note: Outcome denominators are not given in the abstract.

harms.label: Mesh exposure
harms.note: The one-year abstract does not give an exposure numerator.

harms.label: Reoperation
harms.note: The abstract does not quantify reoperations.

reports.label: Three-year final analysis
reports.citation: Gutman RE, Nosti PA, Sokol AI, et al. "Three-year outcomes of vaginal mesh for prolapse: a randomized controlled trial." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2013;122(4):770-777. doi:10.1097/AOG.0b013e3182a49dac
reports.followUp: Three-year questionnaires; blinded POP-Q examination at two or three years

results.measure: Anatomic, symptomatic and combined cure under multiple definitions
results.note: The abstract gives no arm-specific cure rates; this was a planned final analysis after early trial closure.
results.locator: PubMed abstract, Methods, Results and Conclusion

results.note: The P value concerns within-group improvement; abstract does not give arm-specific denominators.

harms.label: Reoperation for recurrent prolapse
harms.note: All three reoperations were in the mesh group.
